## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR should not merge yet. Adding `adopt` entries to the returned changes makes `run` print every adoption message twice. The audit entry is handled correctly: it is appended and kept out of command output.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — `plan` already calls `emit(f"Adopted {name}")` at line 8 as progress output. The new line also appends `{"kind": "adopt", "message": f"Adopted {name}"}`. `run` (`app/cli.py:6-9`) emits every change whose kind is not `"audit"`, so `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, emit)` now emits `["Adopted theme", "Adopted theme"]`. No test calls `run` with an existing setting, which is how this went unnoticed. Should `run` also skip `"adopt"` entries, since `plan` already reported them as progress? If so, could you add a `run` test with an existing setting that asserts `messages == ["Adopted theme"]`? — Every adopted setting is printed twice in command output, which goes against the PR's stated behaviour of keeping adoption progress output while rendering only actionable changes.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `run` skips `kind == "audit"` entries (`app/cli.py:7-8`). The new test `tests/test_planner.py:17-21` checks both that the audit entry is the last returned change and that it does not appear in command output, so it would fail if the audit message were printed.
